key_insight: OQRAM enables private delegated quantum queries by hiding the address access pattern with encrypted, shuffled, and coherently masked QRAM interactions instead of exposing a standard query interface.
engineering_relevance: This reduces the quantum resources required on the client side and offers a practical privacy layer for cloud quantum computing, with an exponential reduction in quantum communication versus local QRAM-style implementations.
method: Offline refresh phase keeps the database encrypted and shuffled.
Online query phase uses coherent address masking via either qPRP or qOTP.
Decoy checks can be added to detect tampering by a malicious server.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the qPRP-based design supports multi-query use and that the protocol achieves an exponential reduction in quantum communication while adding only modest online quantum overhead.
watch_item: Security and efficiency depend on the chosen masking method and the reliability of decoy checks, so real-world deployment will need careful implementation and threat-model validation.
paper_title: OQRAM: Oblivious Quantum Random Access Memory for Securing Delegated Quantum Queries
